To evaluate the range of models trained to fit a scaling law, train or validation loss are most commonly used, but some works consider other metrics, such as ELO score (Jones, 2021; Neumann & Gros, 2022), reward model score (Gao et al., 2023), or downstream task metrics like accuracy or classification error rate (Henighan et al., 2020; Zhai et al., 2022; Cherti et al., 2023; Goyal et al., 2024; Gao et al., 2023).

research_problem_description: Scaling laws describe how model performance and efficiency change with model size and dataset size, offering insights into optimal configurations for deployment. The core challenge is determining the best metrics and methods to fit these laws accurately, considering the variability introduced by different parameters and input variables.
